data.function: re-rank drop: External CAN transceiver: TLE9252VSK (C540122)
data.ruling: The refutation stands, and neither reason for the drop holds. (1) Supply: the requirement "supply from the board's rails" is derived in P2 (FU-A1 P2-R2 out/F.json:459-461, citing IOBoard.md:337-338). It reads "VCC from the 3.3 V logic rail or the 5 V rail". On the TLE9252V, VCC is the transmitter supply on pin 3, 4.5 to 5.5 V (Table 3, P_8.2.2), so it runs from the 5 V rail. VBAT on pin 10 (5.5 to 40 V, P_8.2.1) is a second supply that the requirement does not name. The board's selected source already lies in that range: the DC input is 12 to 20 V and the pack 6.0 to 8.4 V (IOBoard.md, Power table). VIO is 3.0 to 5.5 V (P_8.2.3), so a 3.3 V VIO meets the logic-level requirement. (2) Rule 5: the second-vendor route fails. Digi-Key showed 0 across all three packagings, Active, lead time 22 weeks. A pin-compatible alternate that passes rules 1 to 4 does exist at JLCPCB: the NXP TJA1043T/1J (C140826). NXP is on the S1 list. JLCPCB shows 322,940 in stock with a presale count of 322,842, against a gate of 50 (5 boards x 1 placement x 5 = 25, never under 50; S4, S7). It comes in SOIC-14 with the same pin order: TXD 1, GND 2, VCC 3, RXD 4, VIO 5, EN 6, INH 7, ERR_N 8, WAKE 9, VBAT 10, CANL 12, CANH 13, STB_N 14. Pin 11 differs: it is SPLIT, an optional common-mode output (0.5 VCC in Normal mode, floating in Standby), while the TLE9252V pin 11 is not connected, so it can stay unconnected. The supply ranges match: VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V, VIO 2.8 to 5.5 V, VBAT 4.5 to 40 V. The mode control is the same: EN and STB_N both high give Normal mode, both low give Standby. A transceiver has no firmware registers. Also on JLCPCB: TJA1043T,118 (C95335), 3,006 in stock, presale 2,962. The TJA1043 lifecycle is not read here. The alternate still needs its own P4 verification. TLE9252VSK (C540122) passes rule 4: 196 in stock, presale 196, DSO-14, maker label Infineon Technologies. Scope is function: the ruling concerns this function's supply requirement and its second source, not the part's lifecycle, allowlist or LCSC identity.
